items.title: Health Plans Losing Court Battles in No Surprises Act Cases - MedPage Today
items.reason: This article directly addresses No Surprises Act litigation outcomes, which is core to the topic definition's focus on federal litigation related to enforcement of the law.
items.summary: Health plans are losing court battles in No Surprises Act cases, according to MedPage Today reporting. The article indicates that litigation outcomes are favoring parties challenging or enforcing No Surprises Act provisions against health plans, though the specific cases, courts, rulings, and their implications are not detailed in the excerpt provided. These adverse court decisions may signal shifts in how the Act's balance-billing protections and Independent Dispute Resolution provisions are being interpreted and enforced. Revenue-cycle teams should monitor these litigation outcomes as they may influence how health plans must adjust billing practices and dispute resolution procedures going forward.

items.title: Sentara moves to end Anthem contracts in Virginia
items.reason: This reports a concrete contractual dispute between a major provider system and Elevance/Anthem involving potential network status changes that directly impact patient coverage and revenue-cycle operations; such high-stakes contract terminations constitute actionable payer-provider disputes central to revenue-cycle enforcement dynamics.
items.summary: Sentara Health System has moved to end its commercial, Medicare, and Medicaid contracts with Anthem (Elevance) in Virginia, potentially shifting approximately 380,000 patients to out-of-network status. This contractual action creates significant revenue-cycle implications for Sentara facilities, as termination would affect claims processing, reimbursement rates, and patient financial responsibility under Anthem plans. The dispute is material to revenue-cycle teams because network status changes directly drive claim denial patterns, reimbursement adjustments, and collections complexity across multiple payer programs. Such provider-payer disputes frequently escalate into litigation or regulatory review, particularly when affecting large patient populations across multiple programs.

items.title: Complete Health to pay $14.1M in Medicare Advantage settlement - Fierce Healthcare
items.reason: This reports a Medicare Advantage settlement and penalty against a payer (Complete Health), which is a regulatory enforcement action directly matching the topic definition.
items.summary: Complete Health, a Medicare Advantage plan, has agreed to pay $14.1 million to settle a regulatory enforcement action. The settlement appears to relate to Medicare Advantage compliance or operational issues that triggered CMS or related regulatory action. This directly impacts revenue-cycle teams because Medicare Advantage plan penalties and enforcement actions often stem from claims-payment practices, network management, or member benefit administration issues that affect provider reimbursement and claims processing workflows.
